frontier.hypothesis: Target's `addu $a0,$a2,$zero` (the surviving `ud` register) is created AFTER cse - by reload satisfying the island asm's "r" input operand, or by a local_alloc range split - which is why no plain-C `u32 ud = disc;` spelling can reproduce it (three independent spellings now measured: base if/else, init guard, and hoisted-above-0x400; all either fold the copy or cost the `j`).
frontier.mechanism: s6/E7 + s7/H7.4: cse's make_regs_eqv puts disc and ud in ONE quantity and rewrites every in-block read to qty_first_reg, so exactly one of them keeps consumers. Target has BOTH $a2 (read by the bltz at 0x8002D698) and $a0 (read by the island at 0x8002D6A0 and by the slow-path srlv) carrying live consumers, which no cell of the cse predicate produces. Therefore the second register is post-cse.
frontier.next_probe: On the s7 chassis, dump and read .greg / .dbr (NOT .cse, NOT .jump2) for the slow-path region and locate every copy insn that exists after global_alloc; then read tools/gcc-2.7.2/reload1.c's handling of an asm "r" input whose pseudo is also live across the asm's $12 clobber and across the join, and ask what makes reload allocate a SECOND register for it rather than reading the pseudo's own. If reload is the source, the C-level question becomes what makes the asm operand un-shareable with disc's register - not how to spell a copy.

frontier.hypothesis: Slot 88 (the disc<0 arm) is a reorg.c delay-slot-filling decision, not a jump.c/jump2 one - unchanged from s6, and now the ONLY remaining item besides the ud copy.
frontier.mechanism: s6/E11: .jump carries 9 return-0 blocks and .jump2 carries 1 in every build measured; the 9 copies in both the target and our build are re-materialised by reorg.c filling each `j <label>` delay slot with the instruction at the jump target and redirecting the jump past it. Whether the disc<0 arm gets its own re-materialised copy is therefore a fill_slots_from_thread / relax_delay_slots decision.
frontier.next_probe: Dump the s7 `if (disc < 0) return 0;` variant (banked as rejected/s7-disc-lt0-return0-still-crossjumps-score8-142insns.c) and read its .dbr function region against the s7 base .dbr: find the `j` whose delay slot was NOT filled from the return-0 target (the 2 missing insns) and name the fill_slots_from_thread / relax_delay_slots condition that rejected it.

frontier.hypothesis: E12's law (hard-reg conflict sets are source-controllable through local_alloc block-locals) generalises to the other two residual registers, i.e. `ud` wanting $a0/$4 and `result` wanting $v0/$2 in the disc<0 arm are also conflict-set problems rather than order problems.
frontier.mechanism: global.c global_conflicts counts local_alloc-placed pseudos as live hard regs; find_reg then returns the first hard reg in reg_alloc_order that is neither hard-conflicted nor held by a conflicting allocno. Lengthening or shortening a global's live range over specific block-locals therefore selects its register directly.
frontier.next_probe: For whichever pseudo must land in $a0 once the ud copy survives, compute the REQUIRED hard-conflict set ({2,3} blocked, $4 free) from the .lreg ';; Register N in H.' map BEFORE building, exactly as E12/E13 did for $a2. The whole allocation is now predictable from one .lreg read - use that instead of sampling spellings.
